title: PillarPoint Labs - Launchpad Activation Intake & Runbook Handoff
summary: Initial activation intake for PillarPoint's Pilot: discuss network/VPC pattern, KMS integration, target SLOs, pilot scope (10k requests/day), and runbook handoff. Agreed to run small perf bench next week and share security pack. Some minor transcription noise and mislabels present.
topics: VPC peering and private deployment pattern
KMS/HSM key management and encryption at rest
SLOs: 95th p50 latency goals and throughput expectations
Runbook handoff and next steps for benching
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-06
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~22 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (CSM), Luis (SE), Asha (PillarPoint), Ben (PillarPoint), Riley (PillarPoint)

Auto-summary: Quick kickoff to align on infra patterns and security before pilot spin-up. Agreed to a perf run and to share security artifacts (SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight 30 minutes ish but looks like 20 today, quick intros?
[00:12] Asha: hi yes Asha here, head of ml at PillarPoint, i'll be the primary for model behavior and evals, um hi Ben and Riley are on for infra and security
[00:24] Ben: hey all Ben, platform eng, i'll own network and the VPC connection work
[00:30] Riley: Riley, security lead, hi, we'll want to see encryption flows and audit logs
[00:37] Jordan: great, Samira do you wanna run the agenda?
[00:40] Samira: yeah quick: 1) infra/VPC pattern and peering options, 2) keys and encryption, 3) perf/SLO discussion, 4) runbook and next steps, and time for Qs.
[01:02] Luis: one note up front, when we say private deploy there are a couple flavors—Redwood Hosted VPC peering, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private on-prem package. each has different network needs and timelines
[01:22] Asha: for the pilot we prefer hosted but need VPC peering to keep traffic internal, is that doable?
[01:30] Luis: yes, the hosted VPC peering is standard; we've done similar with a few customers but there are perm configs — subnet routes, NAT, and security groups we'll need. Ben, you'll likely need a couple firewall rules and a CIDR allowlist.
[01:55] Ben: yep that's fine, we run strict egress rules so we'll want the exact IP ranges and an option to route via a transit gateway rather than direct peering if possible
[02:12] Jordan: we'll share the IP blocks and recommended routing. note the peering name in our docs is "Redwood Private Peering" but sometimes SE notes call it "pearl" which is an auto transcript mess, ignore that
[02:30] Riley: on keys—we use AWS KMS today and need to understand if Redwood supports customer-managed keys or HSM integration
[02:40] Luis: Redwood Private supports Customer-Managed KMS keys; for Dedicated and Private you can bring-your-own KMS or integrate with a supported HSM. there may be an additional setup window for key rotation and role trust.
[03:00] Riley: ok we'll need the trust policy example, and do you surface audit logs for all decryption events?
[03:10] Samira: yes audit logs are available, we can send our security pack that includes sample CloudTrail mappings and the SOC2 summary, and we can point to where decryption events appear in the logs
[03:26] Asha: perfect, also curious about data retention—our compliance needs say ephemeral caches only, can we disable prefix caching?
[03:36] Luis: yes caching is configurable—prefix/KV cache can be disabled per-tenant; by default we enable prefix caching to improve cost but we can turn it off for PillarPoint's tenant for the pilot
[03:50] Ben: timeline question—if we go with hosted VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, how long to get up for a small pilot?
[04:00] Jordan: realistic is 2 weeks for networking + key setup if nothing else blocks; if you want Dedicated the procurement and capacity lead time is substantially longer
[04:15] Asha: 2 weeks is good, pilot scope we suggested 10k inference calls/day with p50 latency targets 120ms and p95 under 350ms—are those achievable?
[04:32] Luis: depends on model and token length; for trimmed models and 128-token average we can probably meet p50 ~80-120ms on hosted with small batching, p95 depends on burst patterns. we'd recommend running a 24-hour benchmark to confirm
[04:55] Riley: what about cost model during the pilot? we need a rough monthly estimate for budgeting
[05:02] Jordan: we'll send an estimate based on the pilot profile; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization options that reduce unit cost. note that Dedicated has predictable unit costs but higher commit fees
[05:22] Asha: we plan to use an open Llama-derivative for the pilot — any quantization recommendations?
[05:30] Luis: 4-bit quantization is often a good balance for latency and cost; we can provide quant profiles we've validated. small caveat: some eval metrics degrade slightly so we'll watch quality regressions during the bench
[05:48] Ben: for the runbook handoff—what ops runbooks do you provide out of the box?
[05:54] Samira: we have a starter runbook: deployment steps, failover behavior, canary rollout steps, monitoring thresholds, and incident escalation contacts. we'll drop a runbook template in the shared drive after the call
[06:12] Jordan: and we'll include a checklist: vpc peering, kms trust policy, service account creation, api keys, and sample curl flows for smoke tests
[06:25] Asha: for evals we need deterministic prompt sets and a regression baseline, can you ingest our prompt pack?
[06:35] Luis: yes you can upload a prompt set; we also have built-in eval tooling. for the pilot we recommend a nightly regression run against the baseline and alerting on quality drift
[06:52] Riley: audit & compliance—how do you surface user-level access and RBAC? we need SAML/Sso mapping and role separation
[07:02] Samira: Redwood supports SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role templates. we'll share our SSO configuration guide and a sample attribute map for role mapping
[07:18] Ben: any sticky gotchas with CIDR overlaps? our cloud uses 10.0/8 ranges across VPCs
[07:25] Luis: yes CIDR overlap can cause difficulties with direct peering; in that scenario we recommend using a transit gateway or private link via an intermediary to avoid collisions
[07:40] Asha: can we do a smoke perf run next week? like a 24-hour run to gather p50/p95 and throughput numbers
[07:48] Jordan: yes we'll run a bench with your prompt set; action: we need a sample prompt pack and expected token lengths, and an account person to accept the IP blocks and SAML test user
[08:02] Ben: I'll be the network owner and can respond to the IP blocks; I'll also provision a SAML test user if you share the details
[08:12] Riley: i'll review the security pack and get back with a list of any gaps, likely a short checklist
[08:20] Samira: great, we'll share: 1) security pack + SOC2 summary, 2) IP ranges and peering doc, 3) runbook template, 4) quant profiles and bench spreadsheet
[08:35] Luis: and SE will set up a bench plan; we'll likely ask to run 3 variants — default, 4-bit quant, and a cached variant — to compare latency/cost/quality tradeoffs
[08:52] Asha: competitor question — we've evaluated Anthro-pic and OpenAI, what would you say the main difference is for our use case?
[09:02] Jordan: quick take — Redwood focuses on serving economics and unified runtime across hosting modes; Anthropic/OpenAI are model+API providers, whereas Redwood gives more deployment flexibility and observability. (note: transcription garbled "Anthropic" as "Anthro-pic")
[09:20] Ben: acceptance criteria for pilot—1) p95 under 350ms for typical queries 2) no plaintext persistence in caches 3) SAML in place and logs exported 4) cost estimate within budget
[09:35] Samira: let's recap next steps and owners
[09:42] Jordan: recap—Jordan will send IP ranges and pilot estimate; Samira will share security pack and runbook template; Luis will draft the bench plan and quant profiles; Ben will provision SAML test user and confirm firewall rules; Riley will review security pack and return checklist
[09:58] Asha: and timeline, we agreed to try to stand up networking & KMS in ~2 weeks then run bench starting week 3?
[10:07] Jordan: yes that's the plan, we'll aim to start bench by Jan 20 (two weeks) pending network and key signoff
[10:16] Ben: sounds good, I'll look for the IP list and confirm by EOD Thursday
[10:23] Riley: i'll try to get the initial review back within 5 business days
[10:29] Samira: i'll create the shared folder and drop the starter artifacts by EOD today
[10:35] Luis: any other questions?
[10:38] Asha: none from me, thanks everyone
[10:40] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set a bench kickoff meeting for next Tuesday, goodbye

Notes on transcription quality: some product names and proper nouns mistranscribed (e.g., "Anthropic" as "Anthro-pic", "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood Dedicate"), occasional speaker mislabels (SE lines attributed to "Speaker 1").
